1	# SymPy symbolic integration
2	
3	This task is grounded in the public SymPy documentation for symbolic calculus.
4	The notes below are the offline material needed for this task; the URLs are
5	included only as provenance for the public documentation.
6	
7	## Public API notes
8	
9	The SymPy integrals module documents `integrate(f, x)` as the public call for an
10	indefinite integral of an expression with respect to one variable. The
11	introductory calculus tutorial describes this indefinite-integral use as
12	computing an antiderivative, also called a primitive.
13	
14	The same tutorial documents `diff(expr, x)` as the public derivative operation.
15	For a returned elementary antiderivative `F` of an integrand `f`, the usual
16	calculus consistency condition is that local changes in `F` with respect to the
17	integration variable match `f` away from poles or other singular points.
18	
19	If `integrate` cannot compute a closed form, the tutorial says it may return an
20	unevaluated `Integral` object. The supplied workbench cases are ordinary
21	symbolic expressions for which the public workflow returns evaluated symbolic
22	expressions rather than unevaluated integrals.
23	
24	Relevant public references:
25	
26	- SymPy 1.14.0 documentation, Integrals:
27	  `https://docs.sympy.org/latest/modules/integrals/integrals.html`
28	- SymPy 1.14.0 documentation, Introductory Tutorial, Calculus:
29	  `https://docs.sympy.org/latest/tutorials/intro-tutorial/calculus.html`
